scope_checks.answer: Each phrase's use permission follows its own lexical head. In the apple, the smaller article phrase (headed by the) has Det permission, while the outer NP has argument permission through apple, whose determination requirement is satisfied by the article phrase. The article's exclusion from independent argument use is a separate condition on the article phrase alone; it does not block the outer NP's argument use, since intermediate Head relations within a projection don't require a further argument permission.

evidence.quote: Each phrase's use permission follows its own lexical head.
In \mention{the apple}, the smaller article phrase has Det permission; the outer NP has argument permission through \mention{apple}, whose determination requirement is satisfied.
The article's exclusion from argument use remains a separate condition.
Intermediate Head relations within its projection don't require a further argument permission.

scope_checks.answer: No: in the few people, the phrase headed by few is an internal Mod of the nominal headed by people, not an externally determined phrase. In Det or internal Mod function, ordinary few excludes external determination within its own phrase; the determines the outer nominal (people), and target restrictions apply to that determined nominal. By contrast, in the lucky few, few heads the independently determined NP, and independent few permits definite determination and adjectival premodification; the also permits plural few in the few, since target restrictions extend to a nominal headed by an independent determinative.

evidence.quote: In \mention{the few people}, its phrase is an internal Mod of the nominal headed by \mention{people}; in \mention{the lucky few}, \mention{few} heads the independently determined NP.
